This study proposes a blockchain-based traceability framework integrating the\\n                    <jats:italic>InterPlanetary File System (IPFS)</jats:italic>\\n                    , Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, and a hybrid GM-PBFT consensus mechanism to ensure secure and efficient data sharing across stakeholders. The proposed system combines on-chain and off-chain storage to reduce blockchain overhead while preserving data immutability. A MobileNetV1-based model is incorporated for product quality assessment. Experimental evaluation using Hyperledger Fabric and Ethereum test networks demonstrates improved performance, achieving 99.3% traceability accuracy, 37% faster recall response, and reduced data tampering risk. The results confirm that the proposed approach enhances transparency, scalability, and trust in agri-food supply chains. The proposed system utilizes a hybrid blockchain architecture, combining\\n                    <jats:italic>Hyperledger Fabric (permissioned blockchain)</jats:italic>\\n                    for secure enterprise-level transactions and\\n                    <jats:italic>Ethereum Layer-2 network</jats:italic>\\n                    for scalability and smart contract execution.\\n                  </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-63360-y\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 7]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7546940\", \"title\": [\"Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Scientific Discovery: Autonomous Research, Human Oversight, Accountability, and the Transformation of Knowledge Creation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Agentic artificial intelligence is extending research automation from individual predictions and laboratory operations to …
